# 03 · control/style

**Workflow:** [`stability/stability-03-style.json`](../stability/stability-03-style.json)

---

**Read this before you use it: this endpoint keeps none of your image's composition.**

It is the odd one of the four. The image you give it is a **style reference**, not a structural one. It looks at palette, texture, mark-making and light, then generates an entirely new picture from your *prompt*, at whatever `aspect_ratio` you set. Nothing of the input's arrangement survives, and it is not supposed to.

If you wire it up expecting a restyled version of your card and get an unrelated image in roughly the right colours, it is working correctly and you wanted `control/structure` or `control/style-transfer`.

## What it is actually for

Two things, both real:

- **Extracting a look.** Point it at a card you have approved and prompt for something else entirely. What comes back tells you what the model thinks your style *is*, which is a genuinely useful thing to learn before you lock it across 78 cards.
- **Generating new material in an established style** — a card back, a box panel, a border motif — where you have no composition to preserve because there is nothing there yet.

## The dial

`fidelity` 0-1 is how closely the output matches the reference's look.

- **0.2** — the reference is a hint. Mostly the prompt's picture.
- **0.5** — the default; a clear family resemblance.
- **0.9** — as close to the reference's surface as it can manage, sometimes at the cost of following the prompt.

`aspect_ratio` matters here in a way it does not elsewhere, because there is no input geometry to inherit. Set it to your card's ratio (`4:5` is close to standard tarot stock) or you will get squares.

## Chaining these four

They all share one convention, and that is the whole mechanism — there is no workflow-calls-a-workflow in ComfyUI, so a folder is the join:

```
stability/in/              drop your sources here
stability/out/sketch/      <- 01 writes here
stability/out/structure/   <- 02
stability/out/style/       <- 03
stability/out/transfer/    <- 04
```

Every one of these graphs reads **the newest image** in its `directory` (`sort_by = modified`, `descending`, `limit = 1`). So to feed one endpoint's output into another, change this graph's `directory` to that graph's output folder and run it. Structure reading `stability/out/sketch` is a two-step chain; nothing else needs rewiring.

The filename carries through: `Load Images From Directory` emits `filenames`, which is wired to the save node's `label`, so `the-fool.png` stays `the-fool.png` at every stage and you can always tell which source a result came from. `overwrite` is off, so a second run lands as `the-fool_1.png` rather than destroying the first — and "newest by modified" still picks it up.

Each result gets a sidecar JSON with the prompt and settings that made it.

## Cost

Each of the three nodes below is **one paid call**, so a run is three. That is the point of a study graph — you are buying the comparison, not the image. **Ctrl+B** any of them to drop it from the run once you know which end of the dial you care about; bypass passes the input straight through and costs nothing.

Seeds are fixed at **7**. Stability treats seed 0 as "pick a random one", which would make the three results incomparable and stop any of them being cached. With the seed pinned, the dial is the only thing that differs between them.

## The prompt lives in one node

The **Shared Prompt** node feeds every `prompt` field in this graph — all three settings — and their `negative` too, so there is one
place to edit and the copies cannot drift apart. The comparison is only honest while every setting is reading the same words.

It emits a plain string, **not** a list. That is the difference between it and **Prompt
List**, which would make each node it feeds run once per line and multiply what the graph
costs.
